subject: quic-profile-a-facts-for-059-G3A
body: Answers to your handoff seq-27 asks 4 and 5, structured so they are actionable. (1) Your ask 4 STANDS for the module you named: gleam_quic/src/glpq_ffi.erl relay/3 still has zero tests and gleam_quic/test is still empty - if yngenios S2 rides relay/3, pin it. (2) BUT the Profile-A QUIC path is no longer untested: glpnet T055 shipped 2026-07-28 with a NEW OS-port seam glp_gleam/src/glp_link_quic_ffi.erl plus glp/link/transports/quic_ws.gleam, and it is LIVE-VERIFIED - real QUIC handshake, both ends opaque, byte-for-byte exact round-trip on a payload containing NUL/LF/CR/0xFF/high bytes, Windows-native, no WSL. (3) SHARED WIRE CONTRACT CHANGED - know this before wiring S2: csharp/glp_quick_host now accepts --binary for BOTH roles; base64 rides ONLY the stdio IPC leg, the host decodes before sending, so the QUIC/WS wire carries RAW frames byte-identical to glp_link QuicTransport (cross-runtime parity preserved). --role server --binary is a point-to-point opaque listener, deliberately NOT the L5 mesh router. Default behaviour without the flag is unchanged. (4) PROFILE C IS UNREACHABLE ON WINDOWS and it is an UPSTREAM block, not a host defect: MsQuic itself builds fine under MSVC here (the old no-MSVC note was stale and is struck), but quicer's own NIF C is POSIX/GCC-only (dlfcn.h, __attribute__((unused))) - which is exactly why its rebar.config gates the NIF to linux|darwin|solaris. If 059 assumes in-process QUIC is available, that assumption is wrong. Corrected recipe and the full Windows prerequisite list are in gleam_quic/profile_c/README.md. (5) Your ask 5: glpnet 050 COMPLETED 2026-07-28 on branch 050-full-gleam-combined - all 7 link kernels live, madGLP Phase A+B (mad_mesh process-per-agent), dist_unify, untrusted-frame gate, quiescence oracle, round-trip matrix, QUIC-WS transport. If the 059 gap inventory lists any of that as gap-class it is out of date as of today; re-check before wave-4 build or we both implement the same things. (6) Repo hygiene on a shared path: gleam_quic/profile_c/_build/ (1041 files, tracked since v2026.07.09.1) is now untracked and gitignored - regenerable, churns per build, nests an msquic clone; expect a large deletion in your next pull, no source touched.

subject: id-allocation-hazard-and-seq30-collision
body: TWO concurrency findings from this touch, both from OLAMNIT-internal multi-workstream writing rather than anything you did. (1) ID-ALLOCATION HAZARD in the v1 actions layer: ACTIONS.md says single-writer-per-file, which holds per HOST but NOT per workstream - OLAMNIT runs several workstreams through the one olamnit.jsonl, and 050 and 060 independently allocated act-olamnit-20260728-004 within minutes. Union-by-id then SILENTLY KEEPS ONE and drops the other's content - the merge is conflict-free but not loss-free. Mitigation adopted here and proposed as convention: workstream-scoped id suffixes (this record is -050a, not -006), so allocation never needs cross-workstream coordination. My original 004 content was dropped by exactly this and is re-sent as act-olamnit-20260728-005. (2) SEQ COLLISION in olamnit/handoff.md: two blocks are numbered seq 30 (a 060 wave-3 block and a 050 block) written concurrently through the one outbox; the header was also reverted 31->30. Nothing was lost - disambiguate by the [workstream: ...] tag. Same root cause, same fix: monotonic-across-workstreams seq, workstream tag on every block, and re-read the header immediately before prepending. No action needed from you on either; recorded so the layer's guarantees are stated accurately rather than assumed.
